findings.message:
[P2] Reconcile the 15-minute cap with token-lifetime policy

Lowering `accessTokenMaxTtlMs` to 15 minutes contradicts the current repository decision in `docs/DECISIONS.md:81`, which retains a 15-minute default and a 30-day maximum, and leaves `docs/agent-login.md:86,132` stale. The new authorization-version check already provides the required stale-token rejection, so this global cap breaks callers that request 30-day tokens. It also reduces the normal signing-key overlap to 15 minutes, so pre-cap 30-day tokens, which this patch explicitly leaves at their original expiry, can be invalidated by the next ordinary key rotation. Either keep the 30-day cap and rely on introspection, or update the governing decision and preserve legacy-key overlap before shipping.

src/auth_config.ts:130-131

summary: The versioned revocation flow and end-to-end demotion/deletion coverage meet issue 8, but the unconditional 15-minute cap conflicts with current token-lifetime policy and can invalidate legacy tokens during ordinary key rotation.

evidence: `src/token_service.ts:198-211` stamps `authorizationVersion` on every signed access token, and `src/token_service.ts:288-290` rejects tokens whose version or user no longer matches.

`src/auth_store.ts:971-1054`, `src/auth_store.ts:1116-1134`, `src/auth_store.ts:1352-1356`, and `src/passport.ts:1810-1814` advance revocation for password/credential, role/scope, passkey and logout changes; deletion makes `getUser` return null.
`src/auth_config.ts:131` and `src/token_service.ts:192-196` limit newly issued access tokens to 15 minutes.
`tests/passport_cutover_test.ts:496-635` proves previously valid administrator tokens return 401 after demotion and deletion, plus credential, logout and agent-revocation cases.
